record.original_question: Can Galois extensions of a number field be counted using a new weight function derived from tuning modules?

evidence.quote: Problem 13.3. Count Galois extensions of a number field using a new weight function derived from tuning modules.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. Let $K$ be a number field. For a finite group $G$, classical results in arithmetic statistics study the counting function
$$N(K, G; X) = \#\{L/K \text{ Galois extension inside a fixed algebraic closure} : \mathrm{Gal}(L/K) \cong G,\ |N_{K/\mathbb{Q}}(\mathfrak{d}_{L/K})| \le X\},$$
where $\mathfrak{d}_{L/K}$ is the relative discriminant. More generally, one considers weighted counts of the form
$$N_w(K, G; X) = \sum_{\substack{L/K \text{ Galois} \\ \mathrm{Gal}(L/K)\cong G,\ \mathrm{disc} \le X}} w(L/K),$$
for a weight function $w$ assigned to each Galois extension $L/K$.

Suppose that to every Galois extension $L/K$ with group $G$ one can associate a "tuning module" $T(L/K)$, i.e. a finitely generated module over a suitable arithmetic ring (for instance, a $\mathbb{Z}[G]$-module or an order-module attached to $L/K$) functorially built from $L/K$, and let $w_T(L/K)$ be a numerical invariant extracted from $T(L/K)$ (such as a regulator, an index, or a size of a torsion submodule).

Problem. Define a weight function $w_T$ derived from the tuning modules $T(L/K)$ that produces a meaningful weighted count $N_{w_T}(K, G; X)$ of Galois extensions of $K$, and determine the asymptotic behavior of $N_{w_T}(K, G; X)$ as $X \to \infty$. In particular, exhibit a choice of $w_T$ for which the resulting asymptotic is more tractable, or carries finer arithmetic information, than the standard discriminant-ordered count.
artifact.category_tag: arithmetic statistics of number field extensions
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches do not surface any published asymptotic result implementing a weight function on Galois extensions derived from "tuning modules." Standard literature on counting Galois extensions of number fields uses discriminant or conductor weights and does not address this specific tuning-module weight, suggesting the problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Enumerating Galois extensions of number fields
status_evidence.snippet: Recent surveys on counting Galois extensions of number fields with various orderings, none using tuning-module-derived weights.
status_evidence.claim: Current state-of-the-art counts use discriminant or conductor orderings, not tuning-module weights.

status_evidence.title: Counting Number Field Extensions of Given Degree
status_evidence.snippet: Comprehensive overview of weighted counting techniques for number field extensions.
status_evidence.claim: No mention of tuning-module weight functions in standard treatments.
